lines.text: A hundred frost-wolves. Ash could not hunt a hundred frost-wolves before first thaw. So I did what any reasonable lord would do. I asked the blacksmith.
Raw rimeglass is worth forty crowns, my lord. Worked, it's worth five times that. Lamps, forge-hearts, wards. Southern lords pay anything to stay warm.
Can you work it?
My grandfather could. I've got his notes. Somewhere. Under the goats.
The notes were under the goats. Tobin spent three days and nights at the forge. Nobody told him to sleep. He didn't seem to need it.
On the fourth morning he brought me a lamp. A small iron cage with a sliver of rimeglass inside, glowing a steady, gentle blue.
It'll burn for a year. No oil. No smoke.
I held it up, and the whole hall filled with soft light. Thirty-seven people, crowded inside, went quiet.
That's when I understood. We didn't need a hundred wolves. We needed a buyer.
There's a trader who comes north each winter, my lord. From Vask, across the eastern sea. Sharp as a knife, and twice as honest. Which isn't saying much.
He arrived a week later, in a sleigh painted teal and gold.
Pell Marrow, of the Free City of Vask. Buyer of furs, seller of everything else. And you must be the lord who measured zero.
News travels.
News is my second-best product. So. What have you got for me?
I put the lamp on the table.
For a long moment, Pell Marrow said nothing at all.
Worked rimeglass. In Greyhollow. Who made this?
Me.
I'll give you sixty crowns for it.
Corrow merchants in the capital sell these for three hundred.
You've done your reading.
Chapter four of A Merchant's Guide to Southern Markets. Very dry. Excellent price tables.
Two hundred. And I take every lamp you can make before the spring ships sail.
Two hundred crowns a lamp. Twenty lamps, and the debt was paid.
Deal.
We shook hands. His grip was warm. Warmer than it should have been, he said later, for a man who'd spent six days in a sleigh.
That night, the village celebrated. Bram even smiled, though he would deny it.
I didn't notice Pell watching the villagers. Watching Wren split a log with one swing. Watching an old woman carry two full water barrels as if they were empty.
Interesting place, Greyhollow.
And far to the south, in a house that wanted our river, a letter arrived.
Greyhollow is selling rimeglass? Then the boy might actually pay us.
We can't have that.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter four, coming soon.
